page: Microsoft Azure D372s_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 series, powered by Intel processors and hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 372 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1488.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard general-purpose allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated hardware GPU accelerators.

Storage architecture on the D372s_v7 relies entirely on external volumes, as the instance includes no onboard local ephemeral disk capacity. Persistent I/O and root filesystem operations depend on Azure Premium Storage support. This design delegates persistence and volume durability to external managed disks, prioritizing raw compute and memory consolidation on the host.

With 372 dedicated cores and nearly 1.5 TB of memory, the instance delivers high thread parallelism and memory density within a single virtual machine boundary. This profile minimizes distributed networking overhead for scaled applications. The hardware balance aligns with large-scale relational databases, extensive memory-resident analytics, continuous integration fleets, and high-concurrency web application backends.
